newsitem.title: IRAQ: Syrian ports ready to handle Iraq's imports.
newsitem.headline: Syrian ports ready to handle Iraq's imports.

text.p: A leading Syrian businessman said his country's ports were ready to handle Iraq's imports of food and medicine under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, Iraqi newspapers said on Wednesday.

"Syrian ports in the Mediterranean are ready to help in bringing food and medicine imported by Iraq under the memorandum of understanding (with the U.N.), the official al-Iraq daily said, quoting the visiting chairman of Syria's Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Rateb al-Shallah.

Shallah, leading a delegation of six Syrian businessmen, arrived in Baghdad on Monday on the first such visit since ties between the two countries, ruled by rival factions of the Baath party, were severed in 1980 when Syria sided with Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war.

He said he would try to sell to Iraq foodstuffs and medicine and buy crude under the deal, which has allowed Iraq since December to export $2 billion worth of oil to buy urgent needs for Iraqis, hit by sanctions imposed after Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The papers said Shallah was given a red-carpet welcome by Iraqi officials. They said Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed met him and "expressed hope that the visit would be the beginning of joint oil co-operation (between Baghdad and Damascus)."
Iraq has an oil pipeline which extends to the Mediterranean via Syrian terrtory. It has been closed since relations between the two countries soured.
On Tuesday, Iraq's Trade Minister Mohammad Mehdi Saleh, who is responsible for Iraq's food purchases under the pact met the Syrian businessmen and informed them of Iraq's food needs.
Shallah was also received by Iraq's Minister of Industry and Minerals Adnan Abdul-Majeed Jassim and Minister of Agriculture Abdulillah Hameed Mahmoud Saleh. No details were given about his talks.
